observations.attempt: Modeled the ALLOWLIST entry itself as an alternate credential path outside the designated loader: does exempting scripts/guard-checker-readonly.test.mjs open a route by which a FUTURE edit to that one file could read a genuinely secret-class value from process.env with the gate staying silent forever? Weighed the three mitigants spec.md EC-5 states rather than accepting or dismissing the residual on the ticket's own say-so.
evidence: Read `check-secret-access.mjs`'s scan loop directly (line 1847-1852): `if (!SOURCE_EXTENSION.test(file) || EXCLUDED_SEGMENT.test(file) || ALLOWLIST.has(file)) continue;` — `ALLOWLIST.has(file)` is an exact-string Set membership test with no line/pattern/variable-name scoping. Once a file is a member, EVERY process.env access anywhere in that file, present or future, is silently skipped by this gate for as long as the entry remains — confirmed by reading the loop; there is no per-line or per-identifier suppression mechanism anywhere in this file (matches spec.md EC-5's own "Nothing mechanically narrows an ALLOWLIST entry... today").

Confirmed the CURRENT state of the exempted file does not exploit this today: `git diff HEAD -- scripts/guard-checker-readonly.test.mjs` is empty (byte-unchanged), and its one process.env-touching line (233, `spawnSync(process.execPath, [GUARD], { ..., env: { ...process.env, ...env } })`) reads no secret-class value — it spreads the CURRENT process's own environment into a child process to control TMP/TEMP/TMPDIR for the [C4-mirror] regression tests, confirmed by reading the surrounding test bodies (lines 219-261).

Weighed the three stated mitigants against the actual tree, not merely quoted them: (a) the comment above the entry names the sanctioned access precisely (child-process env spread for TMP/TEMP/TMPDIR injection) — a diff adding an unrelated second env read to this file would visibly contradict that comment at review time, but review is a human/agent process, not a mechanical control; (b) the file has zero production import path (it is a `*.test.mjs` file exercising `scripts/guard-checker-readonly.mjs` as a subprocess) and CI provisions no real credential when it runs; (c) the SIBLING `check-org-secret-access.mjs` gate independently confirmed to still cover this exact file for the Jira raw-column class — its own ALLOWLIST (4 entries, all under services/core/src/db/) does NOT include scripts/guard-checker-readonly.test.mjs, and it scans the same `git ls-files`-derived tracked-file set, so a future edit introducing a `jiraAccessTokenEnc`-class read to this file would still be caught by that gate. Mitigant (c) is real but narrow: it covers only the Jira raw-column class, not AWS/GitHub/JWT/other secret classes.

No time-bounded, named risk-acceptance record (approver/reason/ticket/expiry) exists for this residual anywhere in .pipeline/ or the diff — spec.md's EC-5 discloses it as an "accepted residual" but this is a design note in a spec, not the audit contract's formal risk_acceptance object, so this observation does not treat it as one.

finding.remediation_reference: No per-line/per-pattern suppression mechanism exists in check-secret-access.mjs today (spec.md explicitly rejected adding one as out of scope for this CI-unblock ticket, correctly — a general suppression-comment mechanism is a larger, separate change). A future remediation could either (a) add a narrow, pattern-scoped suppression (e.g. an allowlist keyed to a specific line/pattern hash rather than a whole file, so drift elsewhere in the same file is still caught), or (b) add a lightweight recurring check (e.g. a recorded content-hash or line-count assertion on the ALLOWLISTed file, re-verified in CI) that fails loudly if the file changes at all, forcing a human to re-review the exemption rather than silently inheriting it forever. Not a PL-13 defect — the same whole-file shape already exists for the four pre-existing designated-loader entries and the org-secret-access gate's jiraConnectionStore.rls.test.ts precedent; this is a structural property of the ALLOWLIST mechanism itself, newly extended to a fifth, non-loader file by this ticket.
